SELECTED_INDEX: 6
CONFIDENCE: 0.46
EXPLANATION: 1) Strong C=O stretch at 1724 cm⁻¹ together with an aldehydic C-H Fermi band at 2740 cm⁻¹ indicate a non-conjugated aldehyde.  
2) Dominant aliphatic C-H stretches (2883–2972 cm⁻¹) and CH₂/CH₃ bending at 1462 cm⁻¹ show a saturated alkyl chain.  
3) A pronounced band near 760 cm⁻¹ matches the CH₂ rocking mode (~720 cm⁻¹) characteristic of straight aliphatic chains with four or more −CH₂− units.  
4) Candidate 6 (hexanal, “CCCCCC=O”) uniquely fits: it is a straight-chain saturated aldehyde with sufficient methylene units; other aldehydic candidates contain additional functional groups (ethers, alcohols, amides) that should give strong C–O or N–H bands (≈1050–1300 cm⁻¹ or 3200–3400 cm⁻¹) not prominently observed.
